newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Clark attacks Bolger over APEC plans.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Clark attacks Bolger over APEC plans.

text.p: New Zealand Labour leader Helen Clark on Friday accused Prime Minister Jim Bolger of arrogance after he said he planned to attend an APEC summit in Manila this month if his caretaker government was still in place.

Clark told Reuters there were protocols for what a caretaker government could do in consultation with other parties and the public service had been scrupulous in pointing out what Bolger needed authority for.
"That is why I am frankly absolutely astonished at this arrogance of Bolger's over Manila," she said.
"Quite frankly if APEC can do without (U.S. President) Bill Clinton it can do without the Rhodes scholar from New Zealand," Clark said in a sarcastic reference to the fact Bolger left school aged 15.
When President Clinton was unable to attend APEC last year he did not send his deputy.
Clark had no objection to retiring Trade Minister Philip Burdon going to the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum.
She said reports had said the summit was an opportunity for leaders to meet, renew and extend personal relationships.
"Well why should we waste money on that for a guy who is probably on his way out. I think it is absolutely preposterous."
Bolger has said he and his ministers have the right to attend the forum.
Clark's attack was the first sign of frustration after almost three weeks of uncertainty over who will form the next government.

After an inconclusive general election on October 12, Labour and Bolger's conservative National party have held protracted negotiations with nationalist New Zealand First, which holds the balance of power.
